property_summary: After calling Put(x) from any caller with any payable amount, the reference contract always leaves Acc[caller].balance equal to its previous balance plus msg.value (no reentrant change during Put); removing nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant attacker to reenter during Put and change Acc[caller].balance so the invariant can be violated.

For any caller and any payable amount/unlockTime, after Put returns the caller's recorded balance in c.Acc equals the sum of its prior recorded balance and the msg.value it sent (the reference enforces this via nonReentrant_ preventing reentrant modifications; removing the modifier allows a reentrant attacker to alter the balance during Put and violate this invariant).

For any caller and any payable amount/unlockTime, immediately after Put(...) returns the caller's recorded Acc balance equals the prior recorded balance plus the msg.value sent (reference enforces via nonReentrant_; removing it allows a reentrant attacker to change balance during Put and violate this).

Invariant: for any caller and any payable amount/unlockTime, immediately after Put returns the caller's Acc.balance is at least its prior balance (i.e., Put never decreases the recorded balance); removing nonReentrant_ permits a reentrant attacker to call Collect during Put and decrease the balance, violating this.

For any caller, when calling Put(unlockTime) with some ETH, the reference C (with nonReentrant_) guarantees that after Put returns the contract's recorded Acc[caller].balance equals prior balance + msg.value; removing nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant attacker (in its receive/fallback) to call Collect during Put and reduce Acc[caller].balance, violating that equality for some inputs.

After any successful Put by an externally owned actor, the contract's recorded balance for that actor increases by exactly the sent value (Acc[actor].balance == previous + msg.value); the mutated modifier that clears the lock before the body can allow reentrant behavior that results in a different final recorded balance for some inputs (attacker + calldata + value).

For any caller and deposit value, after calling Put(...) the contract's recorded Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., no unexpected extra deduction or reentrant withdrawal occurs); the mutated modifier that clears the lock before the body allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Put and make Acc[caller].balance not equal previous + msg.value for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit value (where deposit >= MinSum), a Put that completes on the reference always increases Acc[caller].balance by exactly the deposited msg.value (no intermediate reentrant Collect can reduce it during Put); the mutant that clears the lock before the body allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Put so the final stored balance can be less than previous + msg.value.

For every caller and deposit value, after calling Put(...) on the correct contract, the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance equals its previous balance plus msg.value (no reentrant Collect can withdraw during Put); the mutant that resets locked_ before the body allows a reentrant attacker to call Collect during Put and cause Acc[caller].balance to be less than previous + msg.value for some inputs.

For every caller and deposit value, calling Put(...) on the reference always results in the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance being >= previous balance (i.e., Put never causes an immediate reduction of the caller's stored balance); the mutant that clears the lock before the body allows a reentrant Collect during Put which can make the final stored balance smaller, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit value >= 1 wei, calling Put(...) increases that caller's recorded Acc balance by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., Acc[caller].balance == previous + msg.value); the mutant that adds only msg.value/2 breaks this because the recorded balance increases by half the sent value for some inputs.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, after calling Put(...) the contract's recorded Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly the full msg.value (not half); the mutant that stores only msg.value/2 breaks this rule for some deposit values.

For any caller and any deposit value, calling Put increases that caller's Acc.balance by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., Acc[caller].balance == previous + msg.value); the mutant that stores only msg.value/2 violates this for some deposit values.

For any caller and any sent msg.value, after calling Put(...) the public Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly msg.value; the mutant that adds only msg.value/2 violates this for some msg.value (e.g., odd values where integer division loses half), so there exists inputs that make Acc[caller].balance != previous + msg.value.

For any caller and any deposited msg.value, the reference contract always increases Acc[caller].balance by exactly msg.value (so address(c).balance == previousContractBalance + msg.value and Acc[caller].balance == previousAccBalance + msg.value); the mutant that adds only msg.value/2 breaks this because for some msg.value (e.g., odd values or in general) the recorded Acc balance and/or contract balance bookkeeping diverge, so there exist fuzzed deposits where the public Acc getter shows less than the expected increase.

After a successful Put that sets a nonzero balance, a subsequent Collect that meets conditions can be called twice (second call succeeds) on P but the second call is blocked on M (so only one successful Collect is possible).

If a caller with sufficient balance and passed unlock time calls Collect once successfully, then calling Collect a second time (with the same caller and same amount) must not revert on the original contract (P).
If a caller's first call to Collect does not revert, then any immediate subsequent call to Collect (with same caller and same amount) also does not revert on the original contract.
If Collect(call) succeeds once for a caller, then an immediate subsequent Collect(call) from the same caller (with any amount) will not revert on the original contract.
For any caller, if a single call to Collect(...) succeeds (does not revert), then that same call made immediately again (same caller and same amount) also succeeds on the original contract.
